Kuvitus: meren poikkileikkaus. Vasemmall: Illustration: a cross-section of the sea. There is a city on the shore at the left and another at the right, and a submarine cable runs along the seabed from one shore to the other. In a circle in the middle, like a magnifying glass, the glass fibre inside the cable is shown, with a ray of light zigzagging along the core by reflecting from the fibre's edges.
Periaatekuva: veden pohjalla oleva lampp: Schematic picture: a lamp at the bottom of the water sends three rays of light to the water surface at different angles of incidence. The normal to the surface is drawn as a dashed line at each point of impact. On the left the angle of incidence of 30 degrees is smaller than the critical angle: the ray refracts into the air, away from the normal, and a weak part is reflected back into the water. In the middle the angle of incidence is the critical angle, 48.8 degrees: the refracted ray travels along the surface. On the right the angle of incidence of 65 degrees is larger than the critical angle: no light gets into the air, and the whole ray is reflected back into the water, which is total internal reflection.
Periaatekuva valokuidusta, ei mittakaava: Schematic picture of an optical fibre, not to scale. At the top the fibre is cut lengthwise: in the middle the core with refractive index n1, around it the cladding with a slightly smaller refractive index n2, and outermost a plastic protective coating. A ray of light travels in the core in a zigzag: it meets the boundary between the core and the cladding at an angle of incidence larger than the critical angle and is totally internally reflected back into the core each time. At the bottom right the same fibre in cross-section: the core, the cladding and the coating as nested circles.
Periaatekuva, ei mittakaavassa: kaksi sa: Schematic picture, not to scale: two cut stones of the same shape in cross-section. From the top face of each stone the same ray of light comes straight down and meets the lower slanting face at an angle of incidence of 38 degrees. On the left, in diamond, which has refractive index 2.42 and critical angle 24.4 degrees, the ray is totally internally reflected twice and returns upwards out of the top of the stone. On the right, in glass, which has refractive index 1.50 and critical angle 41.8 degrees, the angle of incidence is smaller than the critical angle: most of the light refracts out below the stone, and only a weak part is reflected.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: rajakulma asteina: Graph, to scale: the critical angle in degrees as a function of the refractive index n1 of a substance, when the other substance is air with refractive index 1.00. The curve falls from 90 degrees when n1 is 1.00, first steeply and then more gently. Marked points: water, n1 = 1.33, critical angle 48.8 degrees; glass, n1 = 1.50, 41.8 degrees; diamond, n1 = 2.42, 24.4 degrees.
Kuvitus: hyllyllä on kuitulamppu. Sen ja: Illustration: an optical-fibre lamp on a shelf. A bundle of thin transparent plastic fibres rises from its base and curves in every direction. The fibres do not glow along their sides, but the end of each fibre shines as a bright point.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: rajakulma asteina: Graph, to scale: the critical angle in degrees as a function of the refractive index n1 of a substance, when the other substance is air with refractive index 1.00. The curve falls from 90 degrees when n1 is 1.00, first steeply and then more gently. The horizontal grid lines are five degrees apart and the vertical grid lines are 0.1 apart in refractive index. No points are marked on the graph.
